title: SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds 2026: Up to $100,000 Available to Advance Community-Centred Climate Research and Innovation
summary: Simon Fraser University (SFU) has officially launched the 2026 SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds , providing $100,000 in total funding to accelerate innovative climate research that delivers meaningful impact for communities. Designed to support interdisciplinary collaboration, the funding helps transform promising early-stage ideas into practical climate solutions through partnerships between researchers, students, Indigenous Nations, governments, community organizations, NGOs, and industry. Building on the success of its inaugural funding round, the SFU Climate Innovation (CI) initiative continues to strengthen research-for-impact by investing in projects that address pressing climate challenges while promoting sustainability, resilience, equity, and community engagement. Researchers and graduate students interested in developing innovative climate solutions are encouraged to apply before the extended application deadline of 6 August 2026 . About the SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds The SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds are part of Simon Fraser University s commitment to advancing its strategic climate innovation research priorities. Rather than simply funding research projects, the initiative provides a complete ecosystem of support designed to help interdisciplinary teams move ideas toward implementation, attract future funding, and create lasting societal impact. The program encourages collaboration across faculties and disciplines while placing communities and Indigenous partners at the centre of research design and implementation. For 2026, a total of $100,000 has been allocated across three funding streams: Amplification Grants Catalyst Grants Pollinator Awards Together, these funding streams create a research pathway that nurtures emerging ideas, strengthens partnerships, supports graduate researchers, and positions projects for larger national and international funding opportunities. Why the SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds Matter Addressing climate change requires collaboration across disciplines, sectors, and communities. The Seed Funds recognize that impactful climate solutions emerge when researchers work alongside those most affected by environmental challenges. The initiative focuses on supporting projects that: Promote interdisciplinary collaboration. Strengthen Indigenous-led climate action. Advance community-centred research. Encourage knowledge sharing. Support equitable climate innovation. Generate practical solutions for resilient and sustainable communities. Rather than funding research in isolation, SFU Climate Innovation provides long-term support that helps projects mature into large-scale initiatives capable of attracting significant external funding. Funding Streams Available 1. Amplification Grant The Amplification Grant is designed for interdisciplinary teams seeking to develop major collaborative climate research initiatives. Funding Available Two grants of up to $25,000 each. At least one award will support an Indigenous-led application. Purpose The grants support: Workshops Workshop series Partnership development Research agenda development Cross-sector collaboration Preparation of major grant applications Successful teams are expected to develop ambitious research programs capable of securing future funding from major organizations such as: New Frontiers in Research Fund (NFRF) SSHRC Partnership Grants Horizon Europe Philanthropic organizations Expected Outputs Awardees should produce: Comprehensive interdisciplinary research programs Funder-ready proposals Expanded research partnerships Community-centred climate research initiatives 2. Catalyst Grant Catalyst Grants are intended for interdisciplinary faculty teams already working with established community partners. Funding Available Two grants of $15,000 each. Purpose Catalyst Grants help researchers: Deepen community partnerships. Co-design innovative climate solutions. Strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration. Build pathways toward larger research grants. Projects may also include up to two embedded Pollinator Awards , allowing graduate students to contribute directly to research activities while gaining valuable interdisciplinary experience. 3. Pollinator Award The Pollinator Award supports graduate students participating in Catalyst Grant projects. Funding Available Four awards of $5,000 each. Purpose The award enables graduate students to: Conduct community-engaged climate research. Build interdisciplinary research skills. Gain mentorship from faculty. Participate in knowledge mobilization. Develop science communication skills. Receive grant-writing training. Students are expected to contribute their own research objectives while supporting the broader Catalyst project. Research-for-Impact Supports The Seed Funds provide much more than financial assistance. Award recipients gain access to a wide range of professional supports, including: Convening and Facilitation Delivered through the SFU Morris J. Wosk Centre for Dialogue, helping teams facilitate meaningful collaboration and co-design processes. Partnership Development Supported by the SFU Partnerships Hub, connecting researchers with: Communities Indigenous Nations Government agencies NGOs Industry partners Knowledge Mobilization The SFU Knowledge Mobilization Hub assists teams in ensuring research findings are translated into practical action through: Knowledge exchange Community engagement Research dissemination Impact-focused communication Grant Writing Support Researchers receive proposal development assistance through: Office of Research Services Institutional and Strategic Awards These services strengthen applications for future large-scale funding opportunities. Capacity Building The Community-engaged Research Initiative (CERi) provides training on: Ethical community engagement Indigenous collaboration Community-centred research Cultural competency Partnership development Additional supports include science communication training, networking opportunities, interdisciplinary forums, and communications assistance. Who Can Apply? The program welcomes applications from several categories of participants. Researchers Multi-faculty interdisciplinary teams. Led by SFU faculty members. Working across multiple disciplines. Graduate Students Students seeking: Interdisciplinary research experience. Community-engaged learning. Climate research mentorship. Partners Collaborating organizations may include: Indigenous Nations Community organizations Government bodies NGOs Industry Academic institutions Eligibility Requirements Amplification Grant Applicants should: Lead interdisciplinary research. Develop collaborative climate research agendas. Convene diverse stakeholders. Prepare proposals for major future grants. Catalyst Grant Applicants must: Include faculty from at least two non-adjacent disciplines. Demonstrate established community partnerships. Focus on collaborative climate innovation. Pollinator Award Graduate student applicants must: Be enrolled at SFU. Be linked to a Catalyst Grant. Demonstrate interdisciplinary research. Include equity, diversity and inclusion considerations. Eligible Expenses Funding may support: Student stipends Research activities Community engagement Travel Workshops Knowledge mobilization Convening activities Climate research implementation Ineligible Expenses Funding cannot be used for: Existing administrative costs Personnel costs unrelated to the project Gifts Entertainment expenses Assessment Criteria Applications will be evaluated based on: Interdisciplinary Collaboration Projects should demonstrate meaningful collaboration across multiple disciplines. Community Co-Creation Successful proposals should show authentic partnerships with communities and Indigenous Nations. Innovation Projects should introduce creative approaches to addressing climate challenges. Feasibility Applicants must present realistic implementation plans. Systems-Level Impact Reviewers will assess the project s potential social, environmental, economic, and health benefits. Equity and Inclusion Projects should reflect multiple perspectives and demonstrate reflexive, equitable research practices. Application Process Applications are reviewed by the SFU Climate Innovation Advisory Group, which includes representatives from: SFU faculty Students Government Community organizations Funding agencies Applicants must complete the relevant application form and submit all required documents by email. Important Dates Activity Date Applications Open 1 June 2026 Application Deadline 6 August 2026 (Extended from 31 July 2026) Successful Applicants Announced September 2026 For More Information Applicants are encouraged to visit the official SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds webpage to learn more about the available funding streams, eligibility requirements, downloadable application forms, scoring rubrics, and research support resources. For questions regarding eligibility or the application process, contact: Skye Vallance Program Manager Email: climate_innovation@sfu.ca Prospective applicants should carefully review the appropriate application form and guidance before submitting their proposal to ensure all eligibility and submission requirements are met. Why You Should Apply The SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds provide an outstanding opportunity for researchers, graduate students, and community partners to collaborate on innovative climate solutions that generate meaningful impact. Beyond financial support, recipients gain access to mentorship, grant development assistance, partnership-building opportunities, and knowledge mobilization resources that help transform early-stage ideas into scalable climate initiatives. Whether your focus is Indigenous climate leadership, sustainable communities, AI for climate action, renewable energy, resilience, or interdisciplinary environmental research, this initiative offers the support needed to move your project from concept to implementation. Conclusion The 2026 SFU Climate Innovation Seed Funds represent a significant investment in interdisciplinary climate research that prioritizes collaboration, community engagement, and real-world impact. By supporting researchers, graduate students, and partners working together across disciplines, the initiative helps develop practical solutions that contribute to resilient, low-carbon, and sustainable communities. Interested applicants should begin preparing their proposals early and submit their completed applications before the 6 August 2026 deadline to take advantage of this unique funding opportunity. title: COP31 Call for Proposals: Submit Your Climate Research to the Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) Program Before 31 August 2026
summary: Applications are officially open for the COP31 Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) Program , inviting experts from around the world to submit published research that can help shape international climate policies and accelerate evidence-based decision-making. Researchers, evaluators, policymakers, and climate practitioners working on evidence-based climate solutions now have an exciting opportunity to contribute to one of the world s most significant climate policy platforms. The Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) initiative serves as a platform that connects high-quality scientific evidence with global climate policy discussions during COP31. The program seeks rigorous, published research that provides practical lessons, policy recommendations, and measurable evidence to support climate action across a wide range of thematic areas. If your research has already been published and contributes to addressing climate change, environmental sustainability, resilience, or climate justice, this is an opportunity to present your work to an international audience of policymakers, researchers, development organizations, and climate practitioners. Application Deadline: 31 August 2026 (23:59 UTC−12) About the COP31 Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) Program The Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) program is an evidence-based initiative designed to strengthen climate policy discussions by bringing together high-quality published research from around the world. Unlike traditional conferences that may accept conceptual ideas or preliminary research, E4CA specifically focuses on completed research that has already undergone publication or formal release. This ensures that discussions during COP31 are grounded in credible evidence and proven findings. The initiative encourages collaboration between researchers, evaluators, institutions, development organizations, universities, think tanks, government agencies, and practitioners who have generated valuable insights into climate and environmental action. Selected submissions will contribute to both virtual and in-person sessions held during COP31 in Türkiye , helping bridge the gap between research and real-world climate policy implementation. Why the E4CA Program Matters Climate change remains one of the world s greatest challenges, requiring informed decision-making backed by reliable evidence. The E4CA program aims to: Promote evidence-informed climate policymaking. Highlight successful climate interventions and lessons learned. Encourage collaboration across countries and institutions. Share innovative approaches to adaptation and mitigation. Strengthen dialogue between researchers and policymakers. Showcase high-quality evaluations and scientific findings. Support global implementation of effective climate strategies. By presenting evidence rather than opinions, the program helps ensure climate decisions are based on measurable outcomes and rigorous analysis. What Type of Research Can Be Submitted? The E4CA program only accepts completed and published research . Eligible publications include: Peer-reviewed journal articles Published research reports Officially released evaluations Published analytical studies Completed evidence-based reports Every submission must present findings from one single published publication . The lessons and conclusions submitted must be directly connected to that publication s analytical framework and methodology. Research That Is Not Eligible Certain types of submissions will not be accepted. These include: Unpublished working papers Opinion articles Editorials Concept papers Research proposals Theoretical essays without published evidence Compilations of unrelated findings from multiple reports Research lacking documented methods or evidence Only research supported by documented methodologies, verified data, and published findings will be considered. Thematic Areas for Submission Researchers may submit evidence under one of several climate-related thematic tracks. 1. Adaptation, Resilience Loss and Damage Research focusing on helping communities adapt to climate change while addressing losses resulting from climate impacts. 2. Biodiversity, Forests Rio Synergies Evidence related to biodiversity conservation, forest protection, ecosystem restoration, and links between major environmental agreements. 3. Climate Finance, Institutions Implementation Studies examining climate funding, institutional effectiveness, governance, implementation strategies, and financing mechanisms. 4. Climate Justice, Equity Poverty Research exploring fair climate policies, social equity, vulnerable populations, and poverty reduction through climate action. 5. Climate-Resilient Cities, Infrastructure Water Evidence supporting resilient urban development, sustainable infrastructure, and water resource management. 6. Evaluation, Evidence Climate Action Studies demonstrating how monitoring, evaluation, and evidence improve climate decision-making. 7. Food Systems, Agriculture Food Security Research addressing sustainable agriculture, resilient food systems, and food security under changing climate conditions. 8. Green Industrialization, Transport Economic Transformation Evidence supporting low-carbon industries, sustainable transportation, and economic transformation. 9. Health Systems Climate Research examining climate impacts on healthcare systems, disease prevention, and public health resilience. 10. Indigenous Peoples Local Communities Evidence highlighting indigenous knowledge, local community leadership, and inclusive climate solutions. 11. Mitigation, NDCs Carbon Markets Studies related to greenhouse gas reduction, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), emissions trading, and carbon markets. 12. Oceans, Seas Coastal Systems Research addressing marine ecosystems, coastal resilience, fisheries, and ocean conservation. 13. Powering Climate Action, Electrification Clean Energy Transition Evidence supporting renewable energy, electrification, and clean energy transitions. 14. Technology, Data Geospatial Evidence Research using technology, data analytics, remote sensing, artificial intelligence, GIS, and spatial analysis to support climate action. 15. Youth Education Studies demonstrating how education and youth engagement contribute to climate solutions. 16. Zero Waste Circular Economy Evidence promoting waste reduction, recycling, sustainable production, and circular economic systems. Selection Criteria Submissions will be evaluated based on several important factors. These include: Scientific rigor Policy relevance Quality of evidence Contribution to climate action Methodological strength Clear communication Published findings Analytical consistency The organizers are particularly interested in research capable of informing policy discussions at the international level. Diversity and Inclusion E4CA aims to create an inclusive and globally representative program. The organizers encourage submissions from: Universities Research institutes Governments International organizations Civil society organizations Think tanks Evaluation agencies NGOs Independent researchers Development partners The final program seeks to include diverse institutions, perspectives, geographic regions, and voices. Language Requirements All submissions must be prepared in: English only Submissions in other languages will not be accepted. How to Submit Your Proposal Applicants should follow these steps: Step 1 Complete the official Submission Form . Step 2 Prepare the required submission materials, including: Title Abstract Extended abstract Preferred thematic track(s) Step 3 Submit the completed proposal before: 31 August 2026 (23:59 UTC−12) Late submissions may not be considered. What Happens After Submission? Every proposal undergoes a structured evaluation process. The review includes: Initial Eligibility Screening Organizers first verify that submissions meet all eligibility requirements. Double-Blind Peer Review Eligible proposals then undergo an independent double-blind peer review process to ensure fairness and academic quality. Session Development Accepted submissions will be grouped with complementary research to create meaningful comparative discussions. Sessions may be held: Virtually In person in Türkiye If Your Submission Is Accepted Successful applicants will be invited to: Confirm participation Choose virtual or in-person attendance (where applicable) Collaborate with other presenters in thematic sessions Prepare final presentation materials Panels will also consider: Geographic diversity Gender balance Complementary expertise Final Presentation Deadline Accepted presenters must submit their final presentation: One week before their assigned event. Why You Should Apply Participating in the COP31 Evidence for Climate Action Program offers numerous advantages, including: Present research at an internationally recognized climate policy platform. Share published evidence with global decision-makers. Contribute directly to international climate policy discussions. Network with researchers, evaluators, practitioners, and policymakers. Increase the visibility and impact of your published research. Collaborate with experts from around the world. Support evidence-informed climate action. Participate virtually or in person in Türkiye. APPLY NOW Important Dates Activity Date Applications Open Now Open Submission Deadline 31 August 2026 (23:59 UTC−12) Notification of Accepted Authors After peer review Final Presentation Submission One week before assigned session Contact Information For questions regarding submissions, applicants may contact: Email: e4ca@deval.org Website: www.e4ca.org Conclusion The COP31 Evidence for Climate Action (E4CA) Program represents an outstanding opportunity for researchers and practitioners to ensure their published work contributes directly to global climate policy discussions. By emphasizing scientific rigor, policy relevance, and evidence-based solutions, E4CA creates a platform where research can influence meaningful climate action on an international stage. If you have completed and published research related to climate change, sustainability, biodiversity, clean energy, climate finance, resilience, or any of the other thematic areas, now is the time to share your findings. Submit your proposal before 31 August 2026 (23:59 UTC−12) and become part of the global conversation shaping climate action at COP31. Visit the OFY website for more opportunities on Conferences . title: Gates Foundation Grand Challenges 2026: Up to US$500,000 for AI-Enabled Family Planning Solutions in Sub-Saharan Africa
summary: The Gates Foundation has opened applications for the 2026 Grand Challenges funding opportunity, “AI-Enabled Consumer Engagement to Advance Family Planning.” The initiative will support organisations that can deploy, test and evaluate artificial intelligence-enabled, direct-to-consumer engagement tools designed to improve contraceptive uptake, method continuation and informed contraceptive choice among women and girls of reproductive age in sub-Saharan Africa. Selected projects may receive up to US$500,000 for an implementation period of up to 12 months. The opportunity is open to eligible organisations worldwide, but proposed activities must be implemented in sub-Saharan Africa and applicants must already have an operational user base, intervention cohort or distribution relationship in a target geography. The application deadline is 25 August 2026 at 11:30 a.m. United States Pacific Time. Applicants should review the official Grand Challenges opportunity page , request for proposals, rules, application instructions, budget template and frequently asked questions before submitting. Overview of the Opportunity The initiative seeks practical, scalable and evidence-generating solutions that use artificial intelligence to improve family planning engagement. Successful applicants will not simply be expected to build an AI tool. They must demonstrate how an AI-enabled consumer engagement approach can be deployed through an existing platform, tested with real users and evaluated against meaningful family planning outcomes. Key information includes: Opportunity title: AI-Enabled Consumer Engagement to Advance Family Planning Initiative: Grand Challenges Organiser: Gates Foundation Challenge topic: Artificial intelligence Application opening date: 21 July 2026 Application deadline: 25 August 2026 at 11:30 a.m. U.S. Pacific Time Maximum funding: US$500,000 per project Maximum project period: 12 months Maximum indirect costs: 15% of the total budget, subject to the Foundation’s indirect cost policy Geographic focus: Sub-Saharan Africa Primary target group: Women and girls of reproductive age Proposal-review completion: Expected in October 2026 Estimated project commencement: Late January or early February 2027 Application method: Online submission through the Gates Foundation portal The Foundation has not stated how many projects will be selected. Why This Initiative Has Been Launched Despite substantial investment in family planning programmes across sub-Saharan Africa, many women and girls continue to face unmet contraceptive needs. Access to family planning is influenced by several barriers, including: Lack of accurate information Limited access to personalised counselling Concerns about side effects Misinformation and social stigma Limited access to trained providers Language and communication barriers Weak continuity between awareness and service uptake Lack of confidential spaces for asking sensitive questions Limited follow-up after selecting or beginning a contraceptive method Clinic-based counselling remains important, but it cannot independently provide continuous, personalised engagement to every potential user at the scale and cost required. Digital health platforms have increased the reach of health information. However, many existing systems depend on one-way messages, fixed scripts or rule-based responses. Such systems may deliver standard information but cannot always respond effectively to an individual user’s concerns, follow-up questions and changing circumstances. How Artificial Intelligence Could Improve Family Planning Engagement Recent advances in large language models and conversational AI have created new possibilities for direct engagement with consumers. AI-enabled tools may be able to: Conduct multi-stage conversations rather than providing a single response. Communicate in local languages. Respond to individual questions and concerns. Personalise information according to the user’s situation. Address misconceptions through interactive dialogue. Provide consistent information at a low marginal cost. Support follow-up communication. Guide users towards appropriate family planning services. Operate through public-sector, private-sector or hybrid channels. Integrate with established telecom, health-system, community or commercial platforms. Organisations across sub-Saharan Africa are beginning to use these tools for women’s health and broader consumer-health needs. However, the field still lacks sufficient evidence showing which AI-enabled engagement models produce meaningful family planning outcomes. The Evidence Gap the Challenge Seeks to Address The Gates Foundation is seeking evidence that goes beyond the number of messages sent, users registered or sessions completed. The initiative seeks to understand: Which AI-enabled approaches are most effective. Which tools work best for different categories of users. Whether personalisation improves outcomes. Which prompts or conversational patterns produce stronger engagement. Whether automated follow-up affects method uptake or continuation. How interaction quality should be measured. How AI-generated conversations influence user behaviour. Which approaches do not work or produce weak results. Whether the cost and operational requirements justify the added value. How safety, confidentiality and content accuracy can be protected. Whether successful models can be responsibly replicated and scaled. Without this evidence, investments in AI-enabled family planning platforms cannot be properly compared, improved or expanded. The Central Question The initiative seeks to answer whether AI-enabled, direct-to-consumer engagement can improve: Contraceptive uptake Continued use of a selected contraceptive method Informed method choice Quality of family planning engagement Access to accurate and personalised information Movement from awareness to action Applicants must also help explain which approaches work, for whom they work, why they work and under what operating conditions they are most valuable. Types of Solutions That May Be Considered The Foundation does not require applicants to have an AI platform that has already demonstrated family planning results. Organisations may apply with an existing consumer engagement approach that has a proven record in: Family planning Women’s health Reproductive health Consumer health Digital health Community health Other closely related health areas The proposed AI component may be new. However, the applicant must already have an established user base, intervention cohort or distribution relationship that makes deployment and evaluation possible within the 12-month period. Projects may be delivered through: Government health systems Public-sector digital platforms Private-sector health platforms Telecom networks Community networks Commercial consumer channels Nongovernmental organisation platforms Hybrid public-private delivery models The programme is not intended to finance a platform that still needs to begin building its user base or negotiating access to a distribution channel. Primary Objectives The initiative has four central objectives. 1. Generate Evidence on Impact and Scale Projects should demonstrate whether and how AI-enabled, direct-to-consumer engagement affects: Contraceptive uptake Method continuation Informed method choice User understanding Behavioural outcomes Engagement at scale Applicants must present a credible evaluation design capable of connecting AI-enabled interactions with downstream family planning outcomes. 2. Identify Features of Effective Engagement Projects should determine which elements of an AI-enabled interaction are associated with stronger results. These elements may include: Content personalisation Conversation design Prompt structures Follow-up methods Automated customer journeys Rapid content adaptation Local-language communication Interaction frequency Timing of follow-up messages Referral pathways Human support before or after digital engagement Applicants should develop and test a clear theory of what effective consumer engagement means in their proposed context. 3. Build a Shared Evidence Base Funded work should generate learning that benefits the wider family planning and digital-health field rather than only improving the applicant’s own platform. Possible shared outputs include: Labelled examples of AI-user interactions Conversation taxonomies Interaction-quality rubrics Safety protocols Confidentiality frameworks AI guardrail protocols Content-quality assessment tools Evaluation frameworks Standardised engagement measures Practical guidance for future implementers Applicants should explain how these outputs could help other organisations evaluate and improve AI-enabled family planning engagement. 4. Assess Cost, Feasibility and Added Value Projects must examine the cost and operational requirements of using AI-enabled engagement. Applicants should assess: Implementation costs Technical requirements Staffing requirements Platform costs Monitoring and evaluation costs Feasibility within existing systems Cost compared with alternative engagement models Conditions in which AI adds meaningful value Conditions in which non-AI approaches may be more suitable Budgets should be proportionate to the proposed deployment and evaluation activities. Expected Characteristics of Strong Proposals Competitive applications should combine a credible operational intervention with a rigorous evaluation plan. Strong proposals are expected to: Produce real programme results. Generate learning for the broader field. Use an existing platform or distribution relationship. Operate at sufficient scale to produce meaningful findings. Measure interaction quality rather than only platform activity. Track downstream family planning outcomes. Include appropriate safety and confidentiality protections. Ground AI-generated information in reliable family planning guidance. Demonstrate deep knowledge of the target geography and population. Present a realistic 12-month implementation plan. Use an appropriate and clearly justified budget. Explain how learning will be shared beyond the applicant’s organisation. Eligible Organisations The opportunity is open globally to: Nonprofit organisations For-profit companies International organisations Government agencies Academic institutions Collaborations involving multiple stakeholders are encouraged. Potential partnerships could involve: Technology companies and health organisations Universities and government agencies Telecom operators and family planning programmes Nongovernmental organisations and AI developers Public health institutions and community organisations Research institutions and operational delivery partners Individuals are not eligible to receive funding directly. Organisations classified as individuals for United States tax purposes are also ineligible. Awards will be made to the organisation where the responsible investigator or project lead holds their primary appointment. Geographic Requirements Although eligible organisations may be headquartered anywhere in the world, the proposed intervention must operate in sub-Saharan Africa. Applicants should already have women’s-health or consumer-health intervention cohorts in one or more of the following countries: Nigeria Ethiopia Democratic Republic of the Congo Tanzania Senegal Niger Kenya South Africa Zambia Côte d’Ivoire The Foundation has expressed a preference for solutions targeting: Nigeria Ethiopia Democratic Republic of the Congo Tanzania Senegal Niger Côte d’Ivoire Projects in other eligible sub-Saharan African settings may be considered, but activities outside sub-Saharan Africa will not be funded under this call. Existing User Base and Distribution Requirements Applicants must already have an operational consumer-engagement approach and an established user base or distribution relationship. The existing approach may relate to family planning, women’s health or consumer health more broadly. The Foundation will examine the quality of engagement, not merely the headline size of the platform. Applicants should provide evidence such as: Monthly active users User-retention rates Repeat engagement Completion of health journeys Existing delivery partnerships Reach within the proposed geography Level of interaction with women and girls Established referral or service pathways An applicant with a large registered user base but weak active engagement may be less competitive than an organisation with a smaller but consistently engaged population. Requirements for AI-Generated Health Content AI-generated content must be based on vetted and locally relevant family planning information. Content should align with: National Ministry of Health guidance World Health Organization guidance Relevant national family planning protocols Local clinical and ethical requirements Appropriate language and cultural context Applicants should explain how they will prevent the AI system from providing inaccurate, unsafe or inappropriate information. The proposed safeguards should address: Medical misinformation Hallucinated content Confidentiality Sensitive personal information Harmful recommendations Bias Escalation to human support Referral to qualified services Appropriate consent Protection of vulnerable users Measurement and Evaluation Requirements Applicants must propose an evaluation design that measures both the interaction and the outcomes occurring after it. Relevant measures may include: Quality of AI-user conversations Accuracy and relevance of responses Safety and confidentiality User trust User comprehension Personalisation quality Use of referral pathways Contraceptive uptake Method continuation Informed method choice User retention Comparative cost Operational feasibility Applications should present a clear pathway connecting interaction quality with behavioural or service-delivery outcomes. Projects should investigate not only whether behaviour changed, but also how and why the change occurred. Importance of Human Touchpoints The Foundation recognises that digital engagement does not operate in isolation. Human contact before and after an AI interaction may be important to family planning outcomes. Applicants should therefore describe relevant human touchpoints, such as: Community-health workers Family planning counsellors Call-centre agents Clinic staff Peer educators Referral coordinators Pharmacists Healthcare providers Applications should explain how digital and human engagement will work together. Activities That Will Not Be Funded The Foundation will not support proposals that: Use engagement metrics alone as the principal evidence of effectiveness. Focus only on messages sent, sessions completed or users registered. Lack an existing user base or distribution relationship in a target geography. Propose activities outside sub-Saharan Africa. Are primarily research projects without real-world operational deployment at scale. Spend the funding period primarily acquiring users. Depend on negotiating new platform access after the project begins. Focus mainly on building an untested tool without deployment and evaluation. Offer only incremental improvements. Duplicate work already funded by the Foundation or another Grand Challenges initiative. Lack sufficient safety, confidentiality or content-quality safeguards. Funding Level and Project Duration The Foundation will consider awards of up to US$500,000 for each project. The project term may be up to 12 months. Budgets should be proportionate to: Proposed activities Number of users Target geography Evaluation design Technology requirements Operational scope Expected outputs Indirect costs may be included up to a maximum of 15% of the total budget, subject to the Gates Foundation’s indirect cost policy. The maximum available amount is not an automatic entitlement. Applicants should request only the funding reasonably required to deliver the proposed work. Required Application Components The application consists of three principal elements: Applicant profile and organisational information completed through the online portal. A proposal uploaded in Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format. A budget table and accompanying budget narrative. Applicants should follow the official application instructions . Proposal Length and Formatting The proposal must not exceed two pages. Figures, diagrams and references are included in the two-page limit. The proposal must use: Font size of at least 11 points Aptos, Arial or Times New Roman Single-line spacing Standard character spacing Margins of at least 0.5 inches Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF format Maximum file size of 3MB Applicants should not include a separate cover page. The application system will automatically generate one using the registration information. Applications that do not follow these restrictions may be blocked from submission or review. Recommended Proposal Structure The Foundation recommends dividing the two-page proposal into three sections. 1. Introductory Information Suggested length: Half a page. Applicants should provide: A brief description of the problem being addressed. One or two bold sentences explaining the essence of the proposed solution. 2. Proposal Information Suggested length: One page. Applicants should provide: A clear hypothesis. A concise description of the proposed work. An explanation of how the activities will produce the intended outcomes. The proposed evaluation approach. The relationship between AI engagement and family planning outcomes. 3. Path to Impact Suggested length: Half a page. Applicants should explain: What will happen if the proposed work is successful. How the intervention could generate impact. How the model could be expanded or replicated. How findings could influence the wider field. Budget Table and Narrative Applicants must submit a budget table and narrative of no more than one page. The budget may include: Personnel Subcontracts Subgrants Capital assets and equipment Travel Supplies Other expenses Indirect costs A one-paragraph narrative should explain the major cost drivers and show how the requested resources relate to the planned activities and outcomes. Applicant Webinar A dedicated webinar is scheduled for: Date: 4 August 2026 Time: 7:00–8:00 a.m. U.S. Pacific Daylight Time Format: Online The webinar will provide an overview of the request for proposals and allow potential applicants to ask questions. Interested organisations may register for the webinar . A recording is expected to be added to the official challenge page after the event. Application Review Process Applications will proceed through four main stages. Stage One: Initial Screening Applications will be assessed to determine whether they address the challenge’s central requirements. Proposals may be removed if they: Are unrelated to the challenge. Address specifically excluded areas. Offer only incremental improvements. Duplicate existing Foundation or Grand Challenges investments. Are considered unsuitable for the initiative. Applicants removed during screening may receive a decline notification without detailed feedback. Stage Two: Technical Review Technical leads from the Foundation, and potentially other funding partners, will chair or co-chair the review. Applications may be assessed by internal and external reviewers with expertise in the topic or complementary areas. Applicants should write clearly for a multidisciplinary audience because not every reviewer will necessarily be a specialist in the applicant’s exact technical field. Stage Three: Validation and Final Selection The Executive Committee will validate the review and select proposals for possible funding. The committee may recommend funding subject to changes. These modifications may be negotiated during the award process. Selected organisations may be invited to submit a more detailed proposal and will receive further instructions. Stage Four: Due Diligence and Negotiation The final stage will include: Due-diligence review Discussions with investigators Review of organisational and tax status Negotiation of project modifications Agreement on the budget Acceptance of applicable terms and conditions Main Review Criteria Applications will be reviewed against five principal areas. Existing Reach and Family Planning Relevance Reviewers will consider: Strength of the existing user base User-engagement level Monthly active users or equivalent evidence Existing distribution relationships Relevance to family planning outcomes User-acquisition and retention models Human support surrounding the digital interaction Evaluation and Measurement Rigor Reviewers will assess: The pathway from AI interaction to family planning outcomes Measurement of interaction quality Measurement of downstream outcomes The clarity and testability of the theory of effective engagement Whether the approach goes beyond basic engagement metrics Contribution to Shared Evidence Reviewers will examine whether applicants will produce outputs useful to the broader field, such as: Labelled interaction examples Quality rubrics Taxonomies Safety protocols Confidentiality protocols AI guardrails Evaluation tools Safety, Confidentiality and Content Grounding Reviewers will assess: Alignment with national Ministry of Health or WHO guidance Accuracy of AI-generated information Confidentiality measures Safeguarding processes Appropriate AI guardrails Management of sensitive contraceptive information Organisational Fit and Feasibility Reviewers will consider: Knowledge of the target geography Understanding of the target population Ability to operate at scale Feasibility within 12 months Appropriateness of the budget Realism of the timeline Focus on deployment and evaluation Intellectual Property and Confidentiality Applicants should assume that information submitted to the Foundation will not remain confidential. The Foundation may share application information with: External reviewers Consultants Contingent workers Key partners Co-funders Applicants should not include proprietary or confidential information in proposals, budgets or supporting materials. The Foundation is also required to publish information about awarded funding and may describe selected projects through its websites, press releases or promotional materials. Funded organisations generally retain ownership of intellectual property created through their projects. However, project outputs must be made widely available to the intended beneficiaries under the Foundation’s global-access requirements. These conditions are explained further in the official FAQs . Additional Application Information Applicants should note that: Organisational tax-status information must be provided during registration. The Foundation may request additional tax documentation. Applications may be edited after submission until the deadline. A confirmation email will be issued after successful submission. The identities of potential reviewers will not be disclosed. Applicants cannot request the exclusion of a particular reviewer. Reviewers must disclose conflicts of interest. Unsuccessful applicants may not receive individual feedback. The applicant organisation must accept the applicable terms and conditions before an award is activated. title: African Union Opens Call for National Convenors for the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue: Building a Resilient Africa through Accelerated Women Financial and Economic Inclusion
summary: The African Union Commission (AUC), through its Women, Gender and Youth Directorate (AUC-WGYD), has officially launched an Open Call for National Convenors to organize National and Local Consultations for the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue . This important initiative seeks to strengthen women s financial and economic inclusion across Africa by bringing together women-led organizations, civil society, government institutions, financial institutions, researchers, and development partners to shape policies that will influence Africa s economic future. Organizations with experience in leading national dialogues, facilitating stakeholder engagement, and advancing women s economic empowerment are invited to submit proposals to become officially recognized National Consultation Leads. The selected organizations will play a vital role in ensuring that women s voices, experiences, challenges, and recommendations directly contribute to continental policy discussions during the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue, scheduled for October 2026. Application Deadline: 14 August 2026. About the African Union s 2nd Egumeni Dialogue The African Union recognizes that women s financial and economic inclusion is essential for achieving sustainable development across the continent. This commitment aligns with several major African policy frameworks, including: Agenda 2063: The Africa We Want The Maputo Protocol on the Rights of Women in Africa The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Protocol on Women and Youth in Trade The African Union Strategy for Gender Equality and Women s Empowerment (GEWE Strategy) The African Women s Decade on Financial and Economic Inclusion (2020–2030) The Women and Youth Financial and Economic Inclusion (WYFEI 2030) Initiative These initiatives collectively recognize that women are central to Africa s economic growth and social development. Women across Africa serve as: Entrepreneurs Farmers Traders Innovators Professionals Community leaders Caregivers Small business owners Despite these contributions, millions continue to face barriers that limit their ability to fully participate in economic activities. These barriers include: Limited access to finance Restricted ownership of productive assets Limited access to markets Inadequate digital technologies Land ownership challenges Underrepresentation in leadership Limited social protection The African Union further notes that these challenges disproportionately affect: Young women Rural women Women with disabilities Refugee women Internally displaced women Women working in the informal economy What is the Egumeni Dialogue? The Egumeni Dialogue is a continental platform established by the African Union in 2025 to advance: Policy dialogue Strategic partnerships Collective action Evidence-based policymaking Women s empowerment Gender equality Its objective is to identify practical solutions that remove structural barriers preventing women and girls from fully participating in Africa s economic transformation. A defining feature of the dialogue is its emphasis on ensuring that grassroots voices shape regional, national, and continental policies. Rather than developing policies from the top down, the African Union seeks recommendations that originate from women and communities across Africa. Purpose of the National and Local Consultations The National and Local Consultations form one of the most important components of the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue. These consultations are intended to provide an inclusive platform where women from different backgrounds can: Discuss current economic opportunities Identify barriers preventing financial inclusion Share local experiences Recommend policy solutions Highlight successful community initiatives Influence continental policy outcomes Importantly, the recommendations generated from every participating country will directly inform: Discussions during the continental dialogue Official declarations Policy recommendations Future investment priorities Continental strategies for women s economic empowerment Objectives of the National Consultations The consultations aim to achieve several important objectives. 1. Generate National Evidence Organizations will collect practical evidence regarding the current state of women s financial and economic inclusion. This includes identifying: Existing opportunities Ongoing challenges National priorities Emerging trends 2. Identify Barriers Participants will examine obstacles affecting women s ability to access: Finance Markets Technology Productive resources Entrepreneurship opportunities Decent employment 3. Document Successful Practices Consultations should showcase: Innovative government policies Community-led initiatives Successful development programmes Effective financial inclusion models Entrepreneurship support programmes 4. Facilitate Multi-Stakeholder Dialogue Convenors will create opportunities for collaboration among: Governments Financial institutions Private sector actors Women s organizations Development partners 5. Develop Country-Specific Recommendations Every consultation should conclude with actionable recommendations tailored to national contexts while contributing to the African Union s continental policy agenda. Expected Outcomes Each National Consultation is expected to produce meaningful outputs, including: A comprehensive overview of women s financial and economic inclusion Documentation of innovative and scalable solutions Policy recommendations Stronger national partnerships A detailed Consultation Report summarizing: discussions recommendations priority actions These reports will become official contributions to the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue. Who Can Apply as National Convenors? The African Union invites expressions of interest from organizations with demonstrated experience in organizing inclusive national dialogues. Eligible organizations include: Women-led organizations Women s networks Civil society organizations Business associations Research institutions Social enterprises Other eligible organizations experienced in multi-stakeholder engagement Role of Selected National Convenors Successful organizations will receive official recognition as National Consultation Leads. They will independently organize national consultations while coordinating closely with the African Union Commission. Responsibilities include: Planning and organizing consultations Coordinating logistics Providing technical support Supporting consultation financing Engaging stakeholders Facilitating inclusive discussions Sharing consultation outcomes Nominating one representative to attend the continental Egumeni Dialogue The African Union Commission and its partners will sponsor the participation of one representative from each National Consultation at the continental event. Who Should Participate in the National Consultations? The consultations should involve a broad cross-section of stakeholders, including: Women entrepreneurs Business owners Women farmers Agricultural cooperatives Women s rights organizations Economic justice organizations Young women entrepreneurs Innovators Government representatives Public institutions Banks Financial institutions Microfinance organizations Fintech companies Chambers of commerce Private sector associations Development partners Philanthropic organizations Researchers Academics Policy experts Traditional leaders Community leaders Faith leaders Women with disabilities Organizations representing marginalized groups Rural women leaders Urban women leaders Consultation Formats Organizations may conduct consultations using: Physical meetings Virtual meetings Hybrid formats combining both approaches Proposal Requirements Interested organizations must submit a proposal of no more than two pages outlining: Organizational profile Relevant experience Proposed consultation methodology Stakeholder engagement strategy Inclusion strategy for rural, urban, and marginalized women Proposed implementation timeline Communication and visibility plan Brief budget indicating available resources and requested support Selection Criteria Priority will be given to organizations demonstrating: Strong experience in women s leadership Expertise in financial inclusion Economic empowerment initiatives Experience facilitating policy dialogues Capacity to mobilize stakeholders Strong national partnerships Commitment to evidence-based policymaking Ability to independently organize consultations Geographic, linguistic, and regional diversity across Africa Responsibilities After Selection Selected National Convenors must: Organize one National Consultation. Engage diverse stakeholders. Facilitate inclusive discussions. Share consultation outcomes through communication platforms. Nominate one representative to participate in the continental dialogue. Important Timeline Applicants should note the following dates: Launch of Call: 28 July 2026 Application Deadline: 14 August 2026 Notification of Selected National Convenors: 18 August 2026 National Dialogue Period: August–September 2026 Submission of National Reports: 30 September 2026 2nd Egumeni Dialogue: 19–21 October 2026 How to Apply Interested organizations should submit their applications electronically using the subject line: Application – National Convenor – [Country Name] Applications must include: Proposal (maximum two pages) Organizational profile Certificate of registration (where applicable) Contact details of the lead focal person Applications should be submitted via email to: wgdy@africanunion.org For enquiries: MusimentaM@africanunion.org Organizations Strongly Encouraged to Apply The African Union particularly encourages applications from: Women-led organizations and networks Young women-led organizations Rural and grassroots movements Organizations representing women with disabilities Refugee and migrant women-led initiatives Conclusion The African Union s Open Call for National Convenors presents a significant opportunity for organizations committed to advancing women s financial and economic inclusion to influence continental policymaking. By leading National and Local Consultations, selected organizations will contribute directly to shaping recommendations that support women s economic empowerment across Africa. Through inclusive dialogue, evidence-based recommendations, and strong partnerships, the 2nd Egumeni Dialogue seeks to build a more resilient, inclusive, and economically empowered Africa where women have greater access to finance, markets, technology, leadership opportunities, and sustainable livelihoods. Organizations with the expertise and commitment to convene these important consultations are encouraged to submit their applications before the 14 August 2026 deadline.
